label: D1 after a rewarded common a2->S2 trial (with no unrewarded trial before it), when the agent will choose a2 again, early-to-mid episode
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO/D2) and only when the reward input is 1. It never fires when the previous trial was a1 or a rare transition, so in practice it needs the previous trial to be a2->S2 common and rewarded. The trial before that must also have been rewarded (or lie outside the window), and the agent must go on to choose a2 (the policy logit sits in a moderate a2-preferring band). It is active almost only in episode trials 3-59 and is silent from about trial 60 on, which is presumably a slow drift in hidden state. The unit is a reset-gate coordinate thresholded near its ceiling (activations about 0.003), so it is a binary-like signal for a consistent rewarded a2/S2 streak where the agent stays with a2. The upcoming choice (action at D1) is the agent's own computed decision, not an unobservable outcome; every other term is observed history. Dev F1 0.89, recall 0.999. The remaining false positives are mostly at the window first trial, where earlier history is unknown. Magnitude is near-uniform; I did not check what modulates it.

issues: The core structural claims hold. On the dev split the unit is active only at D1 (0 of 380,619 GO steps and 0 of 380,619 D2 steps) and only when in_rew==1 (0 activations at in_rew 0 or -1). It never fires after a rare previous trial (prev_common==0: 0 of 252,894) or after an a1 previous trial (0 of 422,790). It also never fires when the trial before that was unrewarded: on test, C & tv('prev_reward',-1)==0 gives precision 0.000 over 14,790 predicted steps. The upcoming choice is a1 on only 7 active steps.

The claim that activations are nearly uniform and the unit acts like a binary switch is false. The absolute values are small (mean 0.003, max 0.005), but relative to the max they range from about 0.01 to 1.0, and the variation is systematic. (a) Activation grows with the strength of the a2 preference: choice < -2.5 covers activation quartiles [0.22, 0.49, 0.74, 0.95] (weak to strong). (b) Activation grows with streak length: in windows like r1 -> r1:0.24 -> r1:0.45 it ramps up over successive rewarded a2/S2 trials, and when the trial two back was unrewarded, coverage is skewed to low quartiles [0.19, 0.16, 0.11, 0.00]. (c) Activation fades late in the episode: trials 50-59 cover quartiles [0.53, 0.01, 0, 0], so they carry only weak activations.

The phrase 'moderate a2-preferring band [-4.4, -1.5]' is misleading. -4.44 is the minimum of the choice logit, so the band is simply choice < -1.5, the most strongly a2-preferring third of steps, and stronger preference gives larger activation. Nothing about it is moderate.

The 'silent from trial 60' cutoff is really a gradual decline. Trials 50-59 already have low precision (0.63) and only near-threshold activations. The hard ep_trial<60 term is a proxy for slow hidden-state drift, as the explainer guessed.

There are two systematic false-positive classes. The larger one is the window's first trial (rel -3), where prev_action is -1 and earlier history is unknown: test precision there is 0.59 against 0.88 when prev_action==2. This is a limitation of the data rather than of the unit, and the explainer disclosed it. The smaller class is trials 50-59, covered above.

Using the agent's own logit instead of the realized action improves the fit. Replacing action==2 with choice < -1.5 raises test F1 from 0.877 to 0.915 (precision 0.848, recall 0.994, mass recall 0.999). choice < -1.7 reaches test F1 0.918. Neither version uses future information.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 of a streak of rewarded a2->S2 trials: the previous trial was a2, common and rewarded, and the trial before it was rewarded too. The agent strongly prefers a2 (logit < -1.5). Activation grows with streak length and with the strength of the a2 preference, and fades out by about episode trial 60.
